quote: I do not know anything about the integer solutions of x³ + y³ + z³ = 3 beyond the existence of the four sets (1, 1, 1), (4, 4, -5), (4, -5, 4), (-5, 4, 4); and it must be very difficult indeed to find out anything about any other solutions.
note: Mordell posed the problem in his 1953 paper 'On the Integer Solutions of the Equation x² + y² + z² + 2xyz = n' published in the Journal of the London Mathematical Society (Volume s1-28, Issue 4, October 1953, Pages 500–510). Earlier related work on sums of three cubes appears in Mordell's 1942 paper, but the explicit problem for general integers x³ + y³ + z³ = n was formulated in 1953.
